instrument: THE WIRING, LANDED FOR JAVA — spec + flag + two tables + gate entry + the emission lookup, with the false-binding clause MEASURED

whatLanded.projectIndex_flag: `qualifyTypeWithFile` — the builder also records every dot-joined SUFFIX of the file's directory path plus the declared name (`a/b/src/main/java/org/x/Foo.java` -> `org.x.Foo`). Suffixes rather than one guess at the source root, because the builder is not told where the source root is.
whatLanded.java_spec: `JAVA_DECLARATION_SPEC` (typeNodes class/interface/enum/annotation/record; members method/field/constructor/enum_constant/annotation element; bases superclass/super_interfaces/extends_interfaces) + the flag.
whatLanded.two_tables: `.java` in `PROJECT_INDEX_EXTENSIONS` and `java: mod.JAVA_DECLARATION_SPEC` in `specByLang` (the producer), plus a `java` entry in the gate's `INDEX_SPECS`.
whatLanded.emission: `real-java-analyzer.ts` both import sites read `context.projectIndex.typeKinds.has(moduleName)`: on a HIT the target is the LEAF and the metadata carries `module`; on a MISS the target is byte-for-byte unchanged.

THE_ACCEPTANCE_CLAUSES.false_bindings_MEASURED_at_zero: **RE-SPELLED (bare target + module metadata): 8,730 | TRUE LOCAL 8,730 | FALSE LOCALS 0.** R2's rule (leaf-in-index) produced 1,798 false bindings on this same population; the lookup produces ZERO. This is the clause to run rather than expect, and it was run.
THE_ACCEPTANCE_CLAUSES.the_invariant_measured: **UNCHANGED (target still the module): 25,004 | of which EXTERNAL 23,476.** The external half is unchanged by construction — the code path that would move it is only taken on an index hit — and the audit confirms every unchanged edge that IS project-local is one of the 1,528 below.
THE_ACCEPTANCE_CLAUSES.the_movement: 8,730 of the split's 8,730 LOCAL edges re-spelled. **1,528 true-local edges were NOT moved** (the R4 recall gap) and they are named rather than rounded away: they are imports whose FQN is not in the qualified index — wildcard imports and inner/nested types are the likely classes, and that is a SECOND question.
THE_ACCEPTANCE_CLAUSES.the_gate_arm_and_its_POPULATION: `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts java java 400 --index` -> exit 1, and it printed `project index: USED — 11 repo index(es) (11 built, 0 from cache, 0 damaged) **over 400 file(s)**`. **THE INDEX IS BUILT AND PASSED** (the wiring works in the gate) **but over the 400-FILE SAMPLE**, and the gate's own header says so: an index over a stride sample is not a project index. Its `imports` row (7,799 · resolved 104 · unresolved 7,695) therefore measures THE SAMPLE, not the fix — most imports point at classes outside the sampled 400. The complete-population measurement is the audit above.

A_DEFECT_I_CAUGHT_IN_MY_OWN_WIRING: I had added `.groovy: "groovy"` to `PROJECT_INDEX_EXTENSIONS` while `specByLang` had no groovy entry — which means the lookup would have fallen through to `?? SOLIDITY_DECLARATION_SPEC` and indexed GROOVY declarations with the SOLIDITY spec. **That is exactly the defect this file's own `.scss` comment records from this morning.** `.groovy` was REMOVED, and the removal carries the reason: a lane is wired when BOTH halves exist, not when its extension is listed. Groovy's spec needs its grammar's node names verified first.
prediction_vs_result: PREDICTED: java LOCAL 8,730 -> 7,594 resolved · 812 ambDeclOnly · 324 ambBoth · 0 unresolved; false bindings 0. **RESULT: the re-spelling reaches all 8,730 with 0 false locals** (the ceiling columns themselves need the complete-population gate arm, which the stride cannot give — stated rather than substituted).
